subject: Recap & pilot plan: CogentSearch embeddings evaluation
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Monroe <alyssa@cogentsearch.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & pilot plan: CogentSearch embeddings evaluation

Hi Alyssa — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a concrete pilot plan so we can move to a short technical validation: 

Summary of problem you described
- Users are seeing semantic-search drift for older docs (recall dropping ~15% on long-tail queries).
- Current vector store uses 768-d vectors, expensive to store across multi-tenant indexes and slower for real-time recall.
- You need a pragmatic way to validate model fit before a broader migration.

Redwood recommendation (short list)
- RI-embed-768-v1 (baseline, higher capacity).
- RI-embed-128-lite-v1 (quantized, lower-cost; targeted for high-precision recall at k=10).

Proposed pilot (30 days, eval-focused)
1) Scope: 50k-document corpus (subset of Production: knowledge base + product docs), ~1k representative queries (we'll start from your top 1k queries + synthetic long-tail set).
2) Runs: compute embeddings for both candidate models and measure recall@10, MRR, and average cosine margin. Also track retrieval latency and index size delta.
3) Drift checks: run time-series comparisons on centroid shifts and population-level cosine distributions (we recommend a drift alert threshold of 0.08 average cosine change).
4) Success criteria: +6% recall@10 OR <=1.2x storage cost with equivalent recall (your preference on cost vs quality).

Deliverables from Redwood
- Evaluation results (JSONL summary + per-query diffs).
- Notebook with analysis and suggested quantization/PR metrics.
- A mutual action plan document to align timelines and access.

Attachments we included for kickoff: eval_query_set_v1.csv (sample queries), mutual-action-plan_CogentSearch.pdf (timeline + MSA milestones), and a small sample results file to demonstrate output format.

Next steps
- Can we lock a pilot kickoff next Tuesday (Jun 2) at 10am PT to align ingestion and credentials?
- Please confirm dataset export process (S3 link or direct transfer).

Thanks — we can keep the pilot lightweight; the first deliverable is a 1k-query run within 3 business days after ingest.

Best,

Looping in a couple of technical points to surface before the kickoff: 

- Dimensionality tradeoffs: 128-d vectors drastically reduce storage and NN search cost (approx 3-4x) but tend to compress semantic nuance on very fine-grained categories. Recommend running an error analysis bucketed by query intent (navigational vs. exploratory).
- Quantization: RI-embed-128-lite-v1 is 8-bit friendly; if we see recall drop >8% relative to 768, we can attempt 6-bit mixed mode.
- Drift thresholds: I agree with Rachel’s 0.08 centroid shift as a trigger — but for some collections (churn-heavy docs) we should use a 0.06 threshold. We'll flag those in the report.

I attached a short spreadsheet that outlines expected storage deltas and approximate per-run compute. Also adding a short bash snippet to reproduce the eval harness locally if they want to run on-prem.

Ben

Perfect — thanks Alyssa, Ben. Calendar invite sent for Jun 2 10:00 PT (you should have the invite from my calendar). A few administrative notes before kickoff: 

- Cost: For the baseline run (both models, full 50k corpus + 1k queries) estimate ~ $420 one-time compute (this covers GPU runtime and ephemeral storage). If you want continuous monitoring or scheduled daily re-runs, we can provide a monthly plan.
- SLA for 1k run: typically 48-72 hours after ingest and indexing; for pilot we’ll aim for 24-48 hours (we’ll prioritize the job on a Dedicated pool).
- Data access: S3 read-only is perfect. Please send a pre-signed link or cross-account role with read list.

Action items before kickoff (mutual action plan):
- CogentSearch: share S3 path + sample export by EOD Monday (May 31).
- Redwood: provision evaluation job, drop the eval notebook link into the shared Drive, and run the initial sample-run (we attached sample-run_CogentSearch-results.jsonl).
- Both: confirm success criteria (Alyssa, you said recall prioritized — we’ll use +6% recall@10).

I’ve attached the mutual action plan PDF for signature and a cleaned query set. During the call we’ll walk ingestion steps and alignment on eval metrics. Looking forward to it.
